items.headline: Amos Yee, 27, handed four new charges over 'alarming and racially divisive' online posts
items.summary: Amos Yee was given four fresh charges in court on Aug 26 over online content that police described as alarming and racially divisive. The convicted offender was offered bail of S$15,000.

items.headline: Singapore to ease dialect-film screening rules from September, with Mandarin subtitles required
items.summary: From September, films with full or majority Chinese-dialect content may screen in cinemas without a cap on showings, as long as Mandarin subtitles and a Mandarin-dubbed version are available. The MDDI will also drop dialect limits on subscription TV.

items.headline: Government studying an undersea tunnel to Pulau Tekong, with possible civilian use
items.summary: Singapore is assessing the feasibility of building undersea tunnels to its outer islands, including Pulau Tekong, and may consider opening parts of Tekong to civilian use in future.

items.headline: British man, 26, arrested after allegedly taking a S$350 jacket from a Changi Airport store
items.summary: A 26-year-old British man was arrested after allegedly taking a S$350 jacket from a mannequin at a Changi Airport store; a Polish woman was arrested in a separate case. Police said investigations are ongoing.

items.headline: India opens missile production to private firms, sharing DRDO technology
items.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh approved transferring DRDO-developed technology for all conventional missile systems to Indian industry for domestic production. The move aims to speed missiles from development to mass production and cut import dependence.

items.headline: India pitches its growth story abroad as foreign investors pull money out
items.summary: India is courting global investors for fresh capital as foreign funds retreat from its markets amid student protests and slowing momentum. Even so, its equity capital market is heading for a record month, buoyed by strong domestic demand for new share sales.

items.headline: India's central bank says the economy remains resilient as growth momentum holds
items.summary: In its monthly report, the Reserve Bank of India said robust macroeconomic fundamentals continue to cushion the economy even as inflation runs above target. The rupee traded near 95.7 to the dollar, down about 6.5% this year.

items.headline: India's monsoon toll passes 100 as Assam floods leave at least 87 dead
items.summary: Floods and landslides from this year's monsoon have killed more than 100 people across India since July, with Assam worst-hit at about 87 deaths and over a million people affected. Kerala has recorded at least 15 deaths as relief camps fill.

items.headline: Update: UK energy price cap to rise 4% to GBP1,723 from October as gas prices climb
items.summary: Regulator Ofgem confirmed the household energy price cap will rise about 4% to GBP1,723 a year from October, as the Middle East conflict pushes up wholesale gas and power prices. The increase undercuts Prime Minister Andy Burnham's move to scrap VAT on electricity bills.

items.headline: UK households' inflation expectations jump to 3.9%, the highest since May
items.summary: British households now expect prices to rise 3.9% over the next year, up from 3.4% in July and the highest reading since May, as cost-of-living fears return. Consumer prices rose 2.9% in the year to July, up from a 15-month low of 2.6% in June.

items.headline: Himalayan flash floods kill at least 160 across Nepal and Tibet, hundreds missing
items.summary: An ice-and-rock avalanche unleashed a sudden flood down the Bhote Koshi, killing at least 160 people on both sides of the Nepal-China border and leaving hundreds missing. A mudslide struck China's Gyirong port, cutting roads, power and communications in the Shigatse region.

items.headline: Ukraine says it hit 16 Russian targets, striking a Lukoil refinery and torching a warehouse
items.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine struck 16 targets inside Russia over the past day, including Lukoil's NORSI oil refinery in Nizhny Novgorod. Drone attacks killed at least three people and destroyed a 100,000-square-metre Wildberries logistics centre in Kotovsk.

items.headline: Update: Iran says the Strait of Hormuz stays closed despite a route deal with Oman
items.summary: Tehran said the Strait of Hormuz remains closed even after agreeing shipping-lane coordinates with Oman, insisting Washington first honour a June 17 memorandum. Inbound traffic would use a northern lane in Iranian waters and outbound a southern lane coordinated with Oman.

items.headline: Yemen's Houthis claim an attack on a Saudi oil tanker in the Red Sea
items.summary: The Houthis said they struck the Saudi tanker Amzan off Yanbu, extending a maritime campaign against Saudi assets begun with a July 20 blockade. Saudi Arabia is seeking to form an international coalition to protect Red Sea shipping.

items.headline: Anthropic signs a $45 billion cloud-compute deal with Nscale
items.summary: Anthropic agreed a $45 billion deal with AI cloud provider Nscale, extending an aggressive run of compute commitments that includes pacts with Amazon, AMD and SpaceX. The scale underscores the arms race for AI infrastructure among the leading labs.

items.headline: Stability AI, maker of Stable Diffusion, raises $76 million in fresh funding
items.summary: Stability AI, the company behind the Stable Diffusion image generator, raised $76 million in a Series B round. The funding comes as image- and video-generation startups draw renewed investor interest.

items.headline: Robotics startup Generalist reaches a $3 billion valuation
items.summary: Generalist, a robotics startup, hit a $3 billion valuation after raising about $200 million led by 8VC, according to sources. The round reflects surging investor appetite for physical-AI and robotics ventures.

items.headline: AI-safety startup Alice raises $140 million near a $1 billion valuation
items.summary: Alice, an AI-safety startup that works with partners including Google and Anthropic, raised $140 million, valuing it close to $1 billion. Investors included Apax Digital, SentinelOne and Samsung.

items.headline: Keenable emerges from stealth with $26 million to index the web for AI agents
items.summary: Keenable came out of stealth with $26 million in seed funding led by Accel, building an index of the web tailored for AI agents. The launch adds to a wave of infrastructure startups targeting agentic AI.

items.headline: Nvidia beats again as data-centre revenue jumps 117% to $89 billion
items.summary: Nvidia reported fiscal second-quarter revenue up 106% from a year earlier, with data-centre sales rising 117% to about $89 billion and now making up 92% of the business. It guided to roughly $108 billion in current-quarter revenue, above the $104 billion analysts expected, assuming no China data-centre sales.

items.headline: Salesforce jumps 14% after hours on a beat lifted by an Anthropic-stake gain
items.summary: Salesforce shares rose about 14% in extended trading after revenue of $11.35 billion topped estimates. Net income jumped 87% to $3.53 billion, helped by a $2.6 billion gain on its stake in AI startup Anthropic.

items.headline: CrowdStrike pops 11% after posting its best quarter and raising guidance
items.summary: CrowdStrike climbed more than 11% after hours after fiscal second-quarter revenue rose 26% to $1.47 billion, beating estimates. CEO George Kurtz called it the best quarter in the company's history as it lifted its full-year outlook.

items.headline: S&P 500 ends little changed as core inflation holds at 3.3% before Nvidia
items.summary: US stocks finished roughly flat on Aug 26 after the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, core PCE, rose 0.2% on the month and 3.3% from a year earlier, in line with forecasts. Oil was steady, with Brent near $92 a barrel, as investors held back ahead of Nvidia's after-the-bell results.

items.headline: Jannik Sinner withdraws from the US Open with a knee injury
items.summary: World No. 1 Jannik Sinner pulled out of the US Open as he continues to recover from a right knee injury that has sidelined him since he won Wimbledon in July. His exit reshapes the men's draw, with Carlos Alcaraz set to return from a wrist injury.

items.headline: Svitolina and Monfils reach the US Open mixed-doubles semis
items.summary: Elina Svitolina and Gael Monfils became the first pair into the US Open mixed-doubles semi-finals, edging Katerina Siniakova and Henry Patten 5-4, 4-5, 10-8 in the revamped event at Flushing Meadows.

items.headline: Antonelli to take a Monza grid penalty for an engine change
items.summary: Championship leader Kimi Antonelli will drop at least 10 places at his home Italian Grand Prix after Mercedes fit a new power unit, team boss Toto Wolff confirmed. The race at Monza is on Sept 6.

items.headline: Verstappen's new Red Bull deal to 2030 ends silly-season speculation
items.summary: Max Verstappen has committed to Red Bull through the end of 2030, ending speculation over a switch to Mercedes or McLaren. Mercedes boss Toto Wolff said he was 'not at all' disappointed, while George Russell said his own seat never felt under threat.

items.headline: Inouye telescope captures the sharpest-ever image of the Sun, revealing swirling instabilities
items.summary: The Inouye Solar Telescope in Hawaii returned the highest-resolution visible-light image of the Sun yet, resolving city-sized features and confirming long-hypothesised Kelvin-Helmholtz instability swirls on the surface. The detail could sharpen understanding of solar magnetism and space weather.

items.headline: Study finds Earth microbes could survive at the Moon's south pole
items.summary: A NASA-linked study found that five hardy microorganisms, including Deinococcus radiodurans and Aspergillus niger, could survive in permanently shadowed regions at the lunar south pole. The finding flags a contamination risk for upcoming Artemis crewed missions.

items.headline: Scientists map the neurons that build grammar in the human brain
items.summary: Using wide-scale single-neuron recordings, researchers identified cells across the frontotemporal cortex that encode parts of speech, grammatical relationships and higher-order sentence structure. The left hemisphere was more active than the right in representing this linguistic information.

items.headline: Webb spots an exoplanet whose chemical make-up defies explanation
items.summary: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope observed an exoplanet with an atmospheric composition that current planet-formation models cannot readily explain. The result adds to a growing list of worlds challenging assumptions about how giant planets form.

fun_fact.headline: Sharks are older than trees
fun_fact.body: Sharks are older than trees. The earliest sharks appeared in the oceans around 450 million years ago, tens of millions of years before the first true trees took root on land roughly 385 million years ago. That means sharks have already survived all five of Earth's great mass extinctions.
fun_fact.source: Natural History Museum (London); American Museum of Natural History

puzzle.title: Four from Six
puzzle.body: You have six matchsticks, all the same length. Arrange all six so they form exactly four triangles, where every side of every triangle is one full matchstick - no bending, breaking, or overlapping. How do you do it?
puzzle.approach: Don't assume the shapes have to lie flat on the table.
puzzle.answer: Build a three-dimensional tetrahedron (a triangular pyramid). Lay three matchsticks flat as a triangle, then stand the other three up from its corners to meet at a single point above the centre. The pyramid has four faces, each an equilateral triangle made of three full matchsticks, using six sticks in all.

word_puzzle.title: A-Game
word_puzzle.body: Centre letter A; outer letters C, I, N, O, R, T. Make words of 4+ letters that each include the centre A and use only these seven letters (letters may repeat). One word - the pangram - uses all seven.
word_puzzle.approach: Every word must contain the centre letter A and use only the seven letters shown; letters may repeat.
word_puzzle.answer: Pangram: TRACTION. Other valid words include ARIA, AORTA, ANTIC, CAIRN, CANTO, CARAT, CARTON, RATIO, RATION, ACTION, ACTOR, TAROT, TIARA, ORATION, TRACTOR, CARROT.
